sourceDate.text: 哀帝初即位；元始中呂寬事覺
during Zhu Bo's service under Emperor Cheng

translationRepairs: In those days Xiao Yu, son of General Wang, and Chen Xian, son of Imperial Secretary Wan, were celebrated heirs of the elite, and Zhu Bo numbered among their companions.
In those days Xiao Yu, son of Former General Xiao Wangzhi, and Chen Xian, son of Imperial Secretary Chen Wannian, were celebrated heirs of the elite, and Zhu Bo numbered among their companions.
望之 and 萬年 are Xiao Wangzhi and Chen Wannian. The proposal restores their given names but still omits both surnames.
At that time Xiao Yu, son of the former general Wang, and Chen Xian, son of Imperial Secretary Wan, were famous as sons of dukes and ministers of outstanding talent; Bo was already friends with them.

At that time Xiao Yu, son of former general Xiao Wangzhi, and Chen Xian, son of Imperial Secretary Chen Wannian, were famous as talented sons of dukes and ministers; Zhu Bo was already friends with them.
The fathers are Xiao Wangzhi and Chen Wannian. Restoring only Wangzhi and Wannian would leave both full names incomplete.

The emperor recalled Xue Xuan, restored his title as Marquis of Gaoyang, advanced him to specially advanced rank just below Tutor Shi of Anchang, gave him a palace attendant post, and assigned him to oversee secretariat business.

The emperor recalled Xue Xuan, restored his title as Marquis of Gaoyang, advanced him to specially advanced rank just below his tutor, Zhang Yu, Marquis of Anchang, gave him a palace attendant post, and assigned him to oversee secretariat business.
師 identifies the emperor's tutor, Zhang Yu, Marquis of Anchang, rather than a man surnamed Shi. The proposal's 'Tutor Marquis' is still awkward and obscures the construction.
Four years on, Ai renamed the chancellor grand tutor and reinstated grand minister of works and grand marshal.
Four years on, Ai renamed the chancellor grand minister of education and reinstated grand minister of works and grand marshal.
改丞相為大司徒 renames the chancellorship to grand minister of education (situ); grand tutor would be 太傅.
Four years later Emperor Ai changed the chancellor to grand tutor, and again set grand minister of works and grand marshal.
Four years later Emperor Ai changed the chancellor to grand minister of education, and again set grand minister of works and grand marshal.
大司徒 is grand minister of education, not grand tutor; the literal repair correctly distinguishes it from 太傅.
General of the Right Wang Jiao and forty-four others held: "As Xuan and the others say—it may be permitted."
General of the Right Jiao Wang and forty-four others held: "As Xuan and the others say—it may be permitted."
蟜望 is surname 蟜 plus given name 望, so Jiao Wang; Wang Jiao reverses the name and misreads the surname.
General of the Right Wang Jiao and forty-four others held: "As Xuan and the others say—it may be permitted."
General of the Right Jiao Wang and forty-four others held: "As Xuan and the others say—it may be permitted."
Same naming error in the literal: 蟜望 must be Jiao Wang, not Wang Jiao.
when Sun Qiaoru of Lu slandered his kinsman Ji Xingfu to Jin and threw Lu into chaos, the Annals condemned it harshly.

when Shusun Qiaoru of Lu tried to monopolize the ducal house by slandering his clan elder Jisun Xingfu to Jin, and Jin seized and imprisoned Xingfu, thereby throwing Lu into disorder, the Annals treated the affair as grave enough to record.
The proposal restores both compound surnames and the omitted events, but 重而書之 means the Annals treated the affair as grave enough to record, not simply that they condemned it harshly.

Lu grandee Sun Qiaoru wished to monopolize the ducal house and slandered his agnate elder Xingfu to Jin; Jin seized and imprisoned Xingfu, disordering Lu—the Spring and Autumn thought it weighty and recorded it.

The Lu grandee Shusun Qiaoru wished to monopolize the ducal house and slandered his clan elder Jisun Xingfu to Jin; Jin seized and imprisoned Xingfu, throwing Lu into disorder, and the Spring and Autumn Annals treated the affair as grave enough to record.
叔孫 and 季孫 are the compound surnames Shusun and Jisun. The proposal fixes only Shusun and leaves Jisun omitted, while 重而書之 also needs an accurate subject and sense.
